summary:
CATACLISMO is an interactive 2D and 3D emergency command platform designed to revolutionize wildfire management, tactical planning, and evacuation response. We developed a unified geospatial web application that bridges the gap between satellite detection and on-the-ground operational decision-making.

The project addresses the critical challenge of fragmented data and time-sensitive coordination during fast-moving wildfires. By integrating real-time satellite feeds (MODIS and VIIRS) with predictive fire-spread simulations, CATACLISMO provides emergency responders with immediate situational awareness. The platform models how terrain and weather conditions—such as wind speed and direction—drive fire progression over time, while simultaneously tracking ground and aerial response units, managing alerts, and mapping safe escape routes to designated shelters with precise time and safety margins. Additionally, it features historical fire activity analysis to support long-term prevention and preparedness.

This project is vital because every minute counts during a wildfire crisis. As climate change intensifies the frequency and severity of forest and wildland-urban interface fires, CATACLISMO empowers command centers and communities to anticipate fire behavior, optimize resource deployment, and execute safe, timely evacuations—ultimately protecting ecosystems and saving human lives.
details:
CATACLISMO — AI-Powered Wildfire Prediction & Dynamic Evacuation Platform

 The Problem
 Wildfires are becoming faster, larger, and more unpredictable. During an active emergency, first responders and civilians often lack real-time visibility into how a fire will spread in the coming hours—and static evacuation plans
 can quickly become obsolete or dangerous.

 Our Solution
 CATACLISMO is an end-to-end geospatial intelligence and 3D visualization platform that combines near real-time NASA satellite data with deep learning to forecast wildfire propagation and generate dynamic, life-saving escape routes.

 How We Use NASA Data

 • NASA FIRMS (Near Real-Time): Ingests live active fire hotspots and thermal anomalies onto a unified 1 km × 1 km geospatial grid (EPSG:3035).
 • NASA POWER: Integrates meteorological and rainfall data (alongside Open-Meteo) to feed environmental risk features into our predictive pipeline.

 Core Architecture & AI Models

 • CATA (Fire Spread Forecasting): A 22-channel ConvLSTM2D neural network that predicts 2D fire probability grids, estimated fire arrival times (in hours), and human/animal risk costs.
 • LUCIA (Dynamic Evacuation Routing): A neural routing engine that consumes CATA’s live fire predictions to compute safe, up-to-date escape routes and meeting points.
 • Interactive 3D Globe: Built with React, TypeScript, CesiumJS, deck.gl, and Three.js, giving users and responders an intuitive 3D view of active hotspots, predicted fire fronts, and evacuation paths.
 • Real-Time Backend: Powered by Python (FastAPI), PostgreSQL + PostGIS, and WebSockets for live updates.

 Impact
 CATACLISMO bridges the gap between raw satellite observations and actionable emergency response—helping communities and responders anticipate fire behavior and evacuate safely before routes are cut off.
